sections.title: Basic Concept of Tenses
sections.content: A tense shows the time of an action — present, past, or future. In Level 1, focus is mainly on Simple Past, Present Perfect, Perfect Continuous, and basic sequence of tenses. Identifying time markers is the most important skill.

sections.title: Simple Past vs Present Perfect
sections.content:
Simple Past is used when the time is clearly finished (yesterday, last year, ago). Present Perfect is used when the time is not specific or the action is recent (recently, just, already, yet).

2-3 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify the time word.
Step 2: If the time is finished → use Simple Past.
Step 3: If the time is unspecified or recent → use Present Perfect.

Examples:
1. I completed the work yesterday.
2. I have completed the work recently.

sections.title: Since and For with Perfect Continuous
sections.content:
Perfect Continuous (has/have been + verb-ing) is used for actions continuing over a period of time. 'Since' is used with a starting point (since 2022, since Monday). 'For' is used with a duration (for two years, for five hours).

2-3 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify whether it is a starting point or duration.
Step 2: Use since for starting point, for for duration.
Step 3: Use has/have been + verb-ing.

Examples:
She has been working since 2023.
She has been working for three years.

sections.title: Stative Verbs and Continuous Forms
sections.content:
Stative verbs describe states, feelings, or mental conditions (know, love, believe, seem, understand). They are generally not used in continuous form.

Incorrect: I am knowing the answer.
Correct: I know the answer.

2-3 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify whether the verb shows a state or feeling.
Step 2: If yes, avoid using -ing form.

sections.title: Basic Sequence of Tenses
sections.content:
If the main clause is in the past, the subordinate clause usually shifts to past tense as well.

Example:
He said that he was tired.

2-3 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify the tense of the main clause.
Step 2: If it is in the past, change the subordinate clause to past.
Step 3: Exception — universal truths remain in present (He said that the earth revolves around the sun).

sections.title: Important Time Markers
sections.content:
Yesterday, ago, last year → Simple Past
Recently, just, already, yet → Present Perfect
Since → starting point
For → duration
Always, every day → Simple Present

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Using Present Perfect with 'yesterday'.
2. Confusing since and for.
3. Using stative verbs in continuous form.
4. Not changing tense after a past reporting verb.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Identify time markers first. Finished time → Simple Past. Unspecified or recent time → Present Perfect. Since = starting point. For = duration. Stative verbs are not used in continuous form.

tricks.title: Yesterday Rule
tricks.explanation: If you see yesterday, ago, or last, think Simple Past immediately.

tricks.title: Recently Rule
tricks.explanation: If you see recently, just, already, or yet, think Present Perfect.
tricks.example: She has just finished her homework.

tricks.title: Since vs For Trick
tricks.example: He has lived here since 2020. He has lived here for five years.

tricks.title: Has/Have Been Signal
tricks.explanation: Has/have been + verb-ing indicates Perfect Continuous.
tricks.example: They have been studying for two hours.

tricks.title: Stative Verb Alert
tricks.explanation: Know, love, believe, seem are not normally used in -ing form.
tricks.example: I love music. (Not: I am loving music)

tricks.title: Past Reporting Trick
tricks.explanation: After said, told, asked, the next clause usually shifts to past tense.
tricks.example: He said that he was busy.

tricks.title: Universal Truth Exception
tricks.explanation: Universal or scientific facts remain in present tense.
tricks.example: He said that the sun rises in the east.

tricks.title: Time Word First Strategy
tricks.explanation: Read the time word before choosing the verb form.
tricks.example: She _____ (finish) her work last night. → finished
